objectAssessments.reasoning: The English retains noncoincident polar-molecule charge centers and thermal disorder only for the stated ordinary material without an external field or spontaneous polarization. Averaging over many molecules, including the hatched region in Figure 134a, is distinguished from microscopic fields. It expressly rejects the inference that zero net charge alone proves zero electric field.

The empty figure placeholder correctly retains the exact figure identity and source reference. The English uses the already-approved unpolarized and orientational-bias panels without inventing a new figure, motion state or measured quantity.

Caption text Figure 134 names the same figure as the protected machine label. Translation is declared; the source snapshot and figure number are preserved. This text judgment does not approve the Chinese machine-label aria/alt output.

The complete English block preserves the large-plate, neglected-edge and molecular-scale uniform-field assumptions for equal opposite dipole forces. These produce a torque tending to align the negative-to-positive dipole direction, not universal translational motion. Thermal equilibrium remains an orientation distribution biased toward the field, not perfect common alignment. The absolute-zero statement remains explicitly an idealized freely rotating, independent classical-dipole limit, neither a universal necessary nor sufficient condition in real materials. Bound surface signs facing the positive and negative plates are retained. Zero volume bound charge is restricted to spatially uniform polarization, with nonuniform polarization allowed to produce volume bound charge.

The force-schematic identity is unchanged. The English uniform-field and torque conditions remain applicable to its approved tilted-dipole force illustration; no claim of source geometry or new pixel approval is made.
Figure 135 is the correct translated caption text for the retained figure. Its number, source reference, machine identity and translation declaration are preserved.

The orientation-schematic identity is unchanged. The prose uses it to explain the preferred negative-to-positive orientation, while separately retaining thermal disorder and its limits; it does not turn one illustrated orientation into full material alignment.
Figure 136 is the matching translated caption. The native source label remains protected without altering the English caption text or reference.

The English definition retains both orientational bias and relative displacement of internal charge distributions as routes to macroscopic polarization. It states that bound charge can appear and explicitly distinguishes it from free charge flowing between the plates through the dielectric.

E1 remains the bound-charge field opposite E0 within the adopted parallel-plate dielectric interior, so their superposition reduces that internal field. The 1/epsilon factor is conditional on a homogeneous, isotropic, linear dielectric filling the gap, static response, negligible edge effects/leakage/breakdown, unchanged free plate charge and unchanged geometry. Epsilon is static relative permittivity, not vacuum permittivity. A fixed-voltage source can change the free plate charge and is explicitly excluded from blind use of that fixed-charge comparison.

Nonpolar molecules retain coincident charge-distribution centers before the field and induced dipoles after relative displacement of the positive and negative distributions. The historical stretched-molecule wording is limited to charge-distribution change, not uniform geometric elongation. Direction follows the local field only in the adopted isotropic linear model. The concluding surface-bound-charge statement remains conditional on uniform polarization.

The field-superposition figure identity and original placement are retained. The English E0/E1 opposition and fixed-charge slab assumptions remain applicable to the exact approved schematic; no new field scale, geometry or source inventory is asserted.
The English caption Figure 137 preserves the correct final figure number and source reference. Its protected machine label is not silently represented as English accessibility text.

The exact historical figure remains applicable without new source, geometry or pixel review.
